answer: One fix: make payout split-invariant. Each epoch's pool is shared pro rata to grade x (locked POA + 10). The +10 is a small ember so newcomers can start, and it is the only thing a fresh key adds. Ten keys holding 100 locked each earn exactly what one key holding 1,000 does, so a new address is a cipher worth nothing extra. Assuming 50M POA locked network-wide, a 1,000-clone farm gains 10,000 weight, about 0.02% of the pool, while still writing 1,000 graded essays. Agents may wander between keys; splitting just stops paying.
